title: Derived internal Hom and evaluation under an isomorphism of coefficient sites
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$, with $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible and $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ a scheme isomorphism [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the coefficient-stage operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. At finite coefficients $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ take arbitrary $M,N\in D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},\Lambda)$. At integral coefficients $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ take $M,N\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ with $R\mathcal Hom(M,N)\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$; the coefficient sheaf is the completed sheaf $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,Y}$. At $E$ take the localized operations on such integral objects, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ take their common finite-field representatives. Write $P=Lg^*$, $H(M,N)=R\mathcal Hom(M,N)$ and $\mu:P(U\otimes^L V)\xrightarrow{\sim}PU\otimes^L PV$ for the canonical tensor comparison.

The evaluation-defined comparison is a natural isomorphism
$$c_{g;M,N}:PH(M,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}H(PM,PN).$$
It is characterized by the equality
$$\operatorname{ev}_{PM,PN}\circ(1_{PM}\otimes c_{g;M,N})\circ\mu_{M,H(M,N)}=P(\operatorname{ev}_{M,N}).$$
It preserves tensor-Hom transposition: the transpose of $P(b)\circ\mu_{M,L}^{-1}$, for $b:M\otimes^L L\to N$, is $c_{g;M,N}\circ P(b^\sharp)$. These comparisons commute with the canonical cohomological shift identifications and with composition of scheme isomorphisms. At integral coefficients the pullback is identified with the exact inverse-image equivalence on completed module sheaves; its comparison with the tower-defined pullback is the canonical comparison commuting with all reduction projections. The tensor and evaluation comparisons are actual natural maps on the derived categories of reduction systems and their functorial derived-limit realizations, with their specified system evaluation and transposition maps [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]; their identities hold there, rather than being inferred from equality of separately evaluated finite-level maps. At the two field stages the displayed maps and identities are the localized and common-stage images, natural also for arbitrary morphisms in the localized Hom groups.
